{"task_id": "md-001", "category": "bug", "issue_title": "Angle brackets stay in the output for some autolinks", "issue_body": "Autolinks like `` work, but with some URLs the angle brackets end up in the HTML. From our install docs: >>> mdlite.to_html("Or install from source: ") '

Or install from source: <git+https://github.com/acme/tool.git>

\n' The same happens with `` and ``. Compare ``: it comes out as `

ftp://files.example.com/a.txt

`, the address without the brackets. It is not a clickable link, which is fine, because the README says only http, https and mailto get linked. Expected: URLs like the ones above get the same treatment as the ftp one. ", "solution_files": ["mdlite/escape.py"]}

{"task_id": "md-002", "category": "bug", "issue_title": "Image alt text is escaped twice", "issue_body": "An `&` in an image's description comes out double-escaped in the `alt` attribute: >>> mdlite.to_html("![Tom & Jerry](/img/tj.png)") '

\n' Browsers and screen readers then show "Tom & Jerry". `<` and `>` have the same problem: `![a < b](/img/cmp.png)` gives `alt="a < b"`. Link text and link titles with the same characters look right, and so does the text that is shown instead of an image whose URL mdlite refuses to link. Expected: `alt="Tom & Jerry"`, i.e. the characters escaped once, like everywhere else. ", "solution_files": ["mdlite/render.py"]}

{"task_id": "sr-002", "category": "bug", "issue_title": "Supplier file with a broken discount ladder was imported without complaint", "issue_body": "Our supplier's price list had a typo in the tiers of one product:

    sku,name,unit,price,taxable,tiers
    GLUE-1,Glue stick,each,2.00,true,5:10;20:5

(it should have been `5:5;20:10`). The products import listed no error for that
row, and the product went into the catalog. We only noticed from the invoices:
every quote for 5 or more glue sticks gets 10 % off, 25 of them included, and the
20-unit step is never used.

I'd expect the import to refuse a row like that and report it, the same way it
reports other bad rows, and to import the rest of the file as usual.
", "solution_files": ["stockroom/catalog.py"]}

{"task_id": "sr-003", "category": "feature", "issue_title": "Load a stocktake count from a CSV file", "issue_body": "Once a month we count every shelf. The count ends up in a CSV file like this:

    sku,counted
    PEN-1,97
    BOOK-1,24

Today I record an adjustment by hand for every line and work out each difference
myself. Please add `store.import_stocktake(path)` that does it for the whole file:

- Afterwards, every product listed in the file has exactly the counted number of
  units on hand. Products that are not in the file are left alone.
- Each change shows up in the ledger as one adjustment with the reason
  `stocktake`. If a count already matches, nothing is recorded for that product.
- The file follows the products file's conventions: UTF-8, a header row with
  exactly the columns `sku` and `counted` in any order, SKUs in any case. A file
  that is empty, not UTF-8 or has other columns is refused as a whole with
  `CsvFormatError`, and nothing changes.
- A bad row is skipped and reported with its line number in the file (the header
  is line 1), and the other rows still apply. A row is bad if its SKU is not in
  the catalog, if its SKU was already counted on an earlier line, if the count is
  not a whole number of 0 or more, or if the count is lower than the units already
  reserved for orders.
- It returns the rejected rows as `RowError` records (the type the products import
  reports), in file order. An empty result means every row was applied.
", "solution_files": ["stockroom/csvio.py", "stockroom/store.py"]}

{"task_id": "sr-005", "category": "refactor", "issue_title": "Refactor: one public way to turn order items into catalog products", "issue_body": "Quoting and creating an order both start the same way: take the list of
`(sku, quantity)` pairs, merge repeated SKUs, check the quantities and look every
SKU up in the catalog. Each has its own copy of those steps, and two copies that
must stay in step are easy to break.

Please give this one public home: a method `resolve_items(items)` on the catalog
(the object at `store.catalog`). It takes an iterable of `(sku, quantity)` pairs
and returns a list of `(product, quantity)` pairs: one per distinct SKU, in order
of first appearance, with repeated SKUs (in any case) merged and their quantities
added up, each product being the catalog's current entry for that SKU. Bad input
raises the same errors quoting raises today: an invalid quantity, a malformed SKU,
or a SKU that is not in the catalog.

Quoting and order creation must both go through this method. This is a pure
refactor: nothing a user of the library can observe may change.
", "solution_files": ["stockroom/catalog.py", "stockroom/orders.py", "stockroom/store.py"]}
